unit.title: Python and HTTP APIs
unit.description: requests, GET and POST with JSON, status codes and raise_for_status, timeouts, headers and tokens, pagination loops, retries and backoff, a FastAPI endpoint

cards.definition: The classic Python library for HTTP: requests.get(url), requests.post(url, json=data). The response has status_code, headers and .json() to decode the body.
A response method that raises an HTTPError when the status is 4xx or 5xx. Without it, a 404 or a 500 goes unnoticed and the script carries on with an error body.
requests waits forever by default. Always pass timeout=(seconds) so a slow API cannot freeze your script or your server.
API credentials go in headers, read from environment variables with os.environ, never hard-coded in the script or committed.
Retrying a failed call after waiting longer each time (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s), for temporary errors such as 429, 502 or 503, never for 400 or 401.
cards.example: for attempt in range(5): try the call, else time.sleep(2 ** attempt)

cards.definition: A modern Python framework to build APIs from type hints: it validates the input, converts JSON and generates interactive documentation automatically.

exercises.prompt: Which call sends a JSON body to create a lead?
exercises.explain: json= serializes the dict and sets the Content-Type header. data= would send a form instead.

exercises.prompt: The API answers 500 and the script keeps going with an error page as data. What was missing?
choices: A print of the URL before the call
Converting the response to a string
exercises.explain: raise_for_status turns 4xx and 5xx into exceptions, so the script stops or handles the error explicitly.

exercises.prompt: What is the risk of requests.get(url) with no timeout?
choices: The script can hang forever if the server never answers
The response is never decoded as JSON
Python refuses to run the line
exercises.explain: requests has no default timeout. Production code always sets one.

exercises.prompt: What does this code print if the API returns {"items": [1, 2, 3], "next": null}?
exercises.explain: .json() decodes the body into a dict; data["items"] is a list of 3 items.

code.src:
r = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
r.raise_for_status()
data = r.json()
print(len(data["items"]))

exercises.prompt: Where should the API token come from?
choices: A constant at the top of the script
A comment in the script header
exercises.explain: Environment variables keep secrets out of Git. URLs end up in logs and browser history.

exercises.prompt: Which errors are worth retrying with backoff?
exercises.explain: Temporary overload or gateway errors may pass. A bad request or bad credentials will fail again the same way.

exercises.prompt: How many requests does this loop send for 250 contacts and a limit of 100 per page?
exercises.explain: Pages of 100, 100 and 50, then next is empty and the loop stops.

code.src:
url = "https://api.example.com/contacts?limit=100"
while url:
    r = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
    r.raise_for_status()
    page = r.json()
    save(page["results"])
    url = page["next"]

exercises.prompt: With FastAPI, a parameter typed int in the function signature is validated automatically, and a text value gets a 422 error.
exercises.explain: True. FastAPI uses type hints for validation and documentation. Wrong input never reaches your code.

exercises.prompt: What does GET /items/7 return with this FastAPI app?
exercises.explain: item_id is converted to an int from the URL, so the double is 14.

exercises.prompt: This script crashes when the API is slow, and sometimes hangs. Which line needs fixing?
exercises.explain: No timeout: add timeout=10 (and retries for 503). The rest is sound.
